Race pace is easily 1+ seconds slower than practice recently, just due to pressure of being in an actual race and not wanting to bin it. Rarely overtake anyone on pace, just inheriting positions when others crash out. In a recent GT3 Endurance race I genuinely felt I was in a slower class car.

I haven't been racing anywhere near as much as previous years, so it's a compounding effect of lack of pace -> don't want to race. Endless practice just feels like a job that I'm paying to do.
People not holding their goddam brakes after an incident. And then usually making a sketchy AF re-entry (using that term as they often appear to be unguided missiles!).

Agreed, probably the most humbling part of motorsports. Especially when you truly couldn't have avoided the incident in the first place based on how they come into contact with you.
On the upside, it should all come back to you a lot quicker next time the track is on the schedule. Even new tracks should get easier to learn over time too as you get used to the car
Roger that! The frustration is real, NOT imagined and racing is a hell of a sport sometimes. How do you think you've had to adapt to this problem?
I get it, your friends are driving away down the road and you take forever just figuring out how to get around the track safely. Your confidence spirals, the mistakes compound. Sound familiar? haha.
Thats why i said i understood why it was the way it was. In my perfect world, there would be rating for each vehicle, but that would be awful for lobbies, so i get why it was the way it is
I don't give a freak about my ratings, the only thing I lose sometimes is my willingness to play.... I wish I had more energy in the day after 10 hours of sitting in front of my work computer

I've thought about this too. Have rating be like a per series thing. But then I remembered when League of Legends tried a similar thing, they changed your ranking based on the role you were playing and it led to more player base frustration, lower participation and less quality games.

I'd imagine a similar thing would happen in iRacing. I guess the argument to keeping it like how it is currently is that a higher rated player will learn and adapt much quicker to a new car.

So we are stuck either practicing too much until we finally feel comfortable or we just say "f it idc about iRating" and just drive and have fun. I'm struggling to find a good mix of adopting both approaches and finding a good balance.

I really want to enjoy the C trucks but lately the lobby’s have been full of idiots. Indycar has been kind to my safety and irating but when I want to jump back into trucks i get caught in others stupidity! 

I was especially looking to racing at Gateway (my home IRL track) but even that was ruin for me by fuckheads who can’t take the time to learn proper breaking! 

I still think I can achieve 2k by the end I the year so I can get into cleaner lobby’s but some races make that feel like a pipe dream….

Did a Gen4 lobby at Talladega last weekend. Caution came out and they guy to my right thought he could cut in front of me. He completely misjudged his position, we crashed which force me to take repairs which put me a lap down. Finished with a 9X myself 🤬.
Even better when you’re in the clear lead and a blue flag thinks you’re their biggest rival.

Practicing for an hour or more, getting into a race, and getting taken out before the 1st lap is even over. Then you got another hour before the race runs again. Maybe you have the time to try again, or you have responsibilities and the only thing you got to do was essentially practice for a race you’ll never complete. 

It’s also frustrating when you discover LMP3’s, have a really good week, then the next week the ringmeister series is running GT3’s so now you gotta spend the whole week doing that instead of the new car you just found. Not a real problem, just a tough decision to make.

For me it’s finding a community to be a part of long term.

I know there are a bunch of Discords and leagues out there, but I don’t only race one thing, so the series focused Discords don’t do much for me, and my time zone isn’t opportune for the types of leagues I’d like to run. Furthermore, too many of them are just echo-chambers for complaints and egos.

I’d just like to find a few people that would really like to improve at whatever they are racing that day, are happy to work together, share, and put in some work for a good finish — and aren’t toxic. Heck, if you think that sounds good and are a North American night owl or West Coaster, feel free to comment. If we get a few people, I’ll send Discord invites.

Getting enough iR to consistently place 10th. Then losing it enough to get wins. Repeat forever. 1200iR to 1600iR. Can't seem to just stay in a higher bracket or improve. Maybe i'm just a solid 1500iR racer with no wrecks and safe drivers around me.

Having like 5-6 good races in a row with minimal incidence then having 1 race that erases all that progress due to my own fault or someone with poor racecraft.    Build myself up to 2.7-2.8 sr in B class then one race I’m back down to 2.3 haha.
It gets better with experience trust me. I used to practice tracks in the F4 for days and now with 30 mins-1 hour im all good on GT3s :)

Trail braking. I only race C grade TCR where everyone ahead of me is a god of trail braking apparently. I can see how much later they start braking and still hit apexes clean.

Frustrated from getting sent to the pits in turn 1, but when it’s happened and I’ve been spit out of the pits ahead of the leaders, I’ve really enjoyed how gracious they are as you give em space to pass and run their race cause most backmarkers at this early stage are awful.

Divebombers, people with poor racecraft. They might got some pace, but they got no idea how to behave on the track and what are the written rules.

I don't like iRacing's incident system. My only goal is to drive clean and consistent laps, but when I'm driving cleanly, someone comes up behind me and touches me, and my incident count goes up. This is very frustrating. 

Some drivers seem to think overtaking works like this: I'll cut in front of them at the corner, and they'll have to slow down to avoid hitting me. Most of the time, I have to do that to avoid getting involved in an incident, but it's really frustrating.

In races that start from the grid, there are definitely a few incidents in the first corner, and sometimes there's nothing you can do to avoid them. If you slow down, someone comes up from behind and hits you; if you try to go through the gap, it doesn't work either. Few people don't understand the meaning of the yellow flag.

I generally enjoy racing at the Nürburgring, and the Porsche Cup is my favorite series. I’ve been racing at the Nürburgring non-stop for about two weeks now, and occasionally I make it into the top five, but I never start from the grid. I start from the pit lane, let everyone else go first, and then start from the back. If I can avoid incidents and maintain consistent lap times, I usually end up in the top 10, but I can’t seem to manage the grid start. If I somehow in the top 3, I’m sure to make a mistake in places I’ve never made mistakes before. My goal for now is to generally finish in the top 10, but if I make it into the top 5, I won’t say no :)

That and it has pretty good engine braking so if you completely let up in the middle of a corner it will start to spin. For example at Leguna Seca this week, on turn 4 you can go into it pretty much flat out if you nail it perfectly, but if you lift throttle completely for literally .5 secs you'll make the turn and sometimes even that will slow you down too much. 

Another example is the last turn. If I don't get all my braking done before the turn and I'm fully lifted the car will get really squirrelly. But if I get all my braking done before that turn and then keep like 10-15% in the throttle before I can get on it it's pretty stable. 

And like the guy above you said, having speed in corners in this car helps but there are some corners where that's not possible.

Also just for SA, I'm only like 1700-1800 iR in that car. My fastest lap at Leguna Seca is 1:23:3xx and there are dudes running 22's so I might be doing everything wrong lol

In both for sure. It’s sucks to give it all in quali and then check the results and still be down 2 seconds to the pole sitter. And then in race I can usually make up a few spots because people wreck and I maybe get 1 or 2 passes.
Might be a bit of an annoying reply here, but money. I have so many track and car combos that I could do because of my licenses, but no free tracks as you progress you just have to spend more money.

I've only been racing for about 2 weeks and things are going fairly well. Progress seems faster than I expected, but I came in with some sim experience. I've already got my first win and a couple of podiums and I can learn tracks reasonably quickly, though I still lean on the racing line for some help. I can't really complain too much when I'm on the cusp of a fast track to my C class sports car license within 3 weeks without cheesing the SR by starting in the pits or qualifying low. I use time trials to practice tracks. It earns some SR so you don't have to live or die by lap 1 antics all the time.


I think the thing I find most frustrating is the lack of interesting variety of content at the start. While the content in rookies is good and interesting, as soon as you have access to more, it becomes very limited. I'm not against buying more content exactly, but I have no way to gauge what tracks would be good purchases in the short term. Long term I understand they will come around again, but if I drop $15 for a new track, will I only get a weeks worth out of it for the next month or 2? I have no simple way to tell. To be fair, I haven't investigated too clearly, but I could use something that says, hey, this track will also feature in these races over the next few weeks, it's worth the price!


I think it would add to the variety a bit if races like the M2 rookie and the MX-5 ran on separate tracks each week.


In terms of driving, nerves definitely get me. I feel like my iRating is landing me in the correct splits. I can qualify reasonably high in some races. But then I'll bonehead my way through T1 and ruin my race. It's not always my fault, but either way, it leaves you feeling a bit broken. That being said, I finish every race. 2 minutes in the pits sucks, but you learn something everytime you pick yourself back up and get back in the race as best you can.


My goal is to just be consistent. I don't need to be fastest, I recognise that consistency is the ground floor of racing. If you can do the same lap over and over, you're off to a pretty good start.
Thinking I've got a track nailed down, having the fastest time in open practice, then getting yoinked in to top split and having my feelings hurt

I didn’t say this, but I’m not too far behind the field. I’ll usually pass some slower moving cars and definitely learn quickly how to avoid the crashes when they occur. I appreciate the advice though!!!

I love the Nords, I’ve already done the SR trick. I haven’t given good thought into joining a league or two. I’m trying to get my friend group into AC so I can race them in our own league. I’ll look into it!!

I'm currently howevering around the D 1.5-1.6k lobbies. The race craft in rookie races (mx5, M2) are awful since at the irating you get matched up with rookie ranks. It makes trying to have a clean race nearly impossible.

I've never experiences such bad race craft since I started M2 rookies as a D class since this week PCC is paid track. MX-5 crashes were mostly avoidable since the bad drivers spin on the first lap but M2s there's so many jumpstarts, using people for braking, diveboming and unsafe rejoins. They should really take M2s and put into D class it's a fun race but it's too fast for rookies to handle.
You won't get much racecraft this way. It's better to learn how to be in the pack than avoiding it at all. It might be frustrating but you'll get better.

In qualifying and practice, I never spin but when in a actual race, I drive a bit slower and spin out every corner. I know it’s just more practice but some races, I feel like I’m on ice and others, I’m superglued to the floor. Probably just nerves and after the first spin, frustration settles in.

Youre pushing much too hard then, cap your braking pressure at 80% with the wizard and you'll also lock it up much less often.

Avoiding a spin in f4 is about rolling the throttle, if yiu just punch it with angle in its going to go around. But roll into your throttle at a rate proportional to your steering, less steering more throttle.

My rig, such as it is.

I have a 4yo Lenovo Legion, a Thrustmaster TMX clamped to my desk, T3PA pedals, one 27" monitor, and a kitchen chair.

The worst part is that the RJ-45-ish connector from the pedals likes to come unplugged during a race. It's happened 6-8 times in the 18 months I've had it. I've usually only hurt myself, but I'll never forget the one time I took out the guy in front of me going into turn 1 on lap 1 at Watkins Glen.

I'm working my way towards a decent rig, followed by load cell pedals, followed by a dedicated machine. But man... I hate this setup.
Network issues are frustrating. One moment everything feels normal then all the sudden it feels like Im just a passenger with disconnected inputs.

The fact that last year I was a 3.x SR B license in sports cars. The last 2 seasons have been stress tests trying to maintain that B license as I’m now hovering around 1.5. No matter what I do I can’t seem to get more than a minuscule gain.
Rookie races run every 30 min. So I use it to farm Sr. But some of the ways I lose Sr there could be VERY frustrating.

For me it's struggling to get that last little bit to win, so often. I usually qualify from 2nd-5th, lower if I had a particularly bad qualifying session. On both short ovals and road courses alike, the car on pole tends to just run away and I can't get close enough over time to really do anything, or I get shoved out of the way eventually if I'm leading. At Lime Rock with the street stock last week, I started 2nd, but the guy in first was two seconds faster for the entire race almost and I never got close enough. I started first, but some guy carved his way from 7th, to right behind me, and then executed a bump and run. I recovered after losing 2 positions, got three seconds behind him. He cut the chicane but barely got a slowdown so despite a huge mistake, he still ran away. 

With short tracks specifically I usually just kinda get stuck behind 2nd and 3rd, 1st place runs away. It's really frustrating since I don't really know how to win other than just being faster than I already am or being lucky enough that they don't get several seconds ahead, or wreck.
Doing a pole lap full race led 0x formula Vee and only getting +.06 when I only needed .09 to get out of rookies lol

I’ve accepted the fact I’m a Mx-5 racer because it’s the best way for me to farm irating and massive safety. Especially around the Nordschliefe. God it’s so much fun bouncing away from corner to corner
If I raced more I would be better at it apart from that I don't see anything else.

Yeah i've learned that at low speed there is minimal downforce going over the spoiler/wings, so it can spin if you overrate and apply too much throttle.

Conversely you can be going fast and you can really work the wheel and it feels great.

i have basically plateaued in terms of pace in GT cars. I have gotten as fast as i can while doing the easy things to get better. and now i have a choice: maintain my current pace and get bored (already happening) or, do a lot of work and see how much better i can get and risk turning simracing into a job.

WOW. Pre-race nerves. Elevated heart rate. Fear of losing safety rating and possibly being dubbed a "dirty driver". You're absolutely not alone. What is the exact feeling you have when starting a race, getting mixed up with traffic? How would you describe it?
My nerves act up so hard my braking foot starts shaking and ruins my race
I just got the car last night and I will say I can’t keep the damn thing from spinning out lol. I can drive it smooth but obviously I have no pace. Any time I try to push I just lose it

100% my nerves. Last night I qualified on pole in the Arca series at Lanier. As soon as the green dropped my heart rate spiked, I was shaky, and I couldnt focus on the race. Took me all of 2 laps to lose the back end a bit. Not much but it was enough to drop me to 6th. I was able to keep it together enough for the rest of the race to finish 3rd but still a little disappointed after being on pole.

I’ve mainly been racing stock late models, I’m new to iracing. It takes me a minute to get used to a new track. Every single time without fail once I get the hang of the track and qualify well, I get taken out in the first 5 laps. It’s been so frustrating.

Every time I'm having a clean race, someone decides to dive bomb on the last lap and wrecks me.

Also, light contact is 4x.  Nobody takes damage, nobody spins out, nobody gets pushed off their line.  We're just racing close and hard and BOOM! 12x after a couple laps of that.  Always grinds my gears when that happens and afterwards you and the people you have a close race with are in the chat saying how great the race was.

Lacking pace can really feel terrible, especially when you feel like you're giving it the "full beans"! Do dig in further though - do you feel like your lacking pace in both quali and the race? Or just in one or the other?

Leagues have been a great help for that, forcing me into a race by giving it a deadline. But 1-2 races a week isn't much especially when i'm driving like I want more.

Racecraft for me, I struggle with patience and sometimes make moves I shouldn't when in certain positions, I have great speed but often make silly mistakes during the race, also my heartrate is usually really high at the start of races, so the nerves get to me too on occasion.
